verses.1: And Rehobam Shchemah went out, for Shchemah came out with all of Israel to be king.
verses.2: And when Jerubbaal, son of Nebat, heard this, he still remained in Egypt. He had fled from King Solomon’s reign. So Jerubbaal settled in Egypt.
verses.3: And they sent for him, and he came. Jeredam and all the people of Israel came forward and spoke to Rehabam, saying:
verses.4: Your father made our lives difficult; now, please ease the burden of your father’s harsh demands upon us. Let us no longer bear the heavy responsibilities that he placed on us, and let us serve you instead.
verses.5: And he said to them, “Go away for three days, and then come back to me.” So the people went away.
verses.6: And King Rehoboam asked the elders who had stood before Solomon’s face during his lifetime, “How can you advise me to return this people to their former ways?”
verses.7: They said to him, “If today you become a servant of this people, and they serve you and speak to you words of kindness, then you will have servants for all your days.”
verses.8: And he abandoned the advice of the elders who had advised him, and he also ignored the advice of the children who had grown up with him. They stood before him, but they were not given any advice at all.
verses.9: And he said to them, “What are you suggesting? Please settle this matter with this people. They have told me, ‘Let’s be merciful to this people, for your father has given us this land.’”
verses.10: And the children who had grown up with him said to him, “Say this to this people: ‘Your father has treated us harshly, but you are too lenient towards us.’” They said this to him, “Young man, you are much more generous than your father.”
verses.11: And now, my father has burdened you with heavy loads. But I will add to your burdens yet more. My father will take them away from you through hardships. And I will also take them away from you through suffering.
verses.12: And Jerubbaal and all the people went to Rehobam on the third day, when the king said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
verses.13: And the king treated the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the elders who offered him guidance.
verses.14: And he spoke to them according to the advice of the children, saying, “My father has covered your heads with dust. But I will remove that dust from your heads. My father has cast you out into the wilderness, but I will rescue you from there.”
verses.15: And the king did not hear the people’s cries, because they were in a state of distress before Jehovah. This was so that he could carry out what Jehovah had said through his brother Shelemiah to Jehudah son of Nethaniah.
verses.16: And all of Israel saw that the king had not listened to them. So the people decided to take action against the king. They said, “What do we get from David’s inheritance? It doesn’t belong to the descendants of Isai. Now, look at your house, King! Let Israel go back to their own homes.”
verses.17: And the children of Israel, who lived in the cities of Judah, were ruled by Rehoboam.
verses.18: And King Rehoboam sent Adonijah to rule over the people. All of Israel mourned over him. King Rehoboam then decided to go up to Jerusalem on his chariot.
verses.19: And Israel sinned in the house of David, up to this very day.
verses.20: And when all the Israelites heard that Jeroboam had returned and called for him to be appointed as king over all Israel, it was not because of the house of David and Judah alone. It was for the sake of the entire Jewish people.
verses.21: Rehoboam went to Jerusalem. He gathered all the people of Judah together, along with the commanders of the army—one hundred and twenty thousand men. They were ready to fight against the Israelites, in order to restore Rehoboam, son of Solomon, as king over them.
verses.22: And God said to Shemaiah, “I will speak through you.”
verses.23: Say to Rehobam, son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the houses of Judah, and to the people in general:
verses.24: So said Jehovah: “Do not fight with our brothers, the children of Israel. Let each person go back to his own home. For from me will come this thing. They listened to Jehovah’s words and went back home as Jehovah commanded.”
verses.25: And Jerubbaal built Shechem on the mountain of Efrath. He settled there, and then he went away from there. After that, he built Penuel.
verses.26: And Yeravam said in his heart, “Now, the kingdom will return to the house of David.”
verses.27: If this people were to go and offer sacrifices in the house of Jehovah in Jerusalem, then their hearts might return to their king, Rehoboam, king of Judah. Then they would kill me and return to Rehoboam, king of Judah.
verses.28: And the king ordered that two golden calves be made. He said to them, “Rejoice over Jerusalem! Behold, your God, Israel, has raised you up from the land of Egypt.”
verses.29: And he placed the one in the house of El, and gave the other to Dan.
verses.30: And this became a sin. The people went before him until they reached Dan.
verses.31: And he built the house of mourning, and he made altars from among the people who were not descendants of Levi.
verses.32: And Jeroboam made a festival on the eighth day of the month, after thirteen days. It was a festival in Judah. He also set up an altar in the Temple of God for the worship of idols. He also appointed priests from among the people who were chosen by God to serve there.
verses.33: And he mounted the altar that he had made in the house of God. This happened on the fifteenth day of the eighth month. He celebrated a festival for the Israelites. Then he mounted the altar to burn incense there.
